root.name: Old Indian Defense: Janowski Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 d6 3. Nc3 Bf5

overview: Black develops the bishop to f5 before playing ...e6 or ...e5, so that it stays outside the pawn chain. White usually plays 4.Nf3 Nbd7 5.g3 or 4.f3 with e4, gaining space, and Black develops with ...e6, ...Be7 and ...O-O or plays ...e5. The position is a quiet space-against-development struggle.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with e4, f3 or g3 and Bg2
Attack the f5 bishop with Nh4 or Qb3 and gain a tempo
Keep a space advantage in the centre

black_ideas.idea: Keep the bishop outside the pawn chain and play ...e6 or ...e5
Challenge the centre with ...c5 or ...e5 at the right moment

typical_structures.structure: White c4/d4/e4 centre against Black ...d6 and ...e5
Black set-up with bishop on f5 and pawns on d6 and e6

character.notes: Quiet development battles with no early tactics; Black's position is solid, if slightly passive.

gambit.notes: No sacrifice in the main lines; 4.e4 (Grinberg Gambit) is a rare exception.

soundness.notes: Sound; White has a small space edge at most.

structure.notes: White's centre is in tension with Black's ...d6/...e5; flexible.

approach.notes: A sensible sideline that strong players play occasionally; standard.

level.notes: Plans are clear and there is little theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Grinberg Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 d6 3. Nc3 Bf5 4. e4
sublines_that_differ.how: White offers the e4 pawn for a lead in development, which Black may take with ...Nxe4.

character.reason: Quiet development with a safe Black structure.

gambit.reason: No material is given in the main lines.

approach.reason: A respectable sideline, played at times by strong players.

plans.reason: White tries to use the extra space in the centre.
